chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Al-Wassafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
It was among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whispered to Musa (peace be upon him): He said, 'O Musa! Honour the beggar with a small gift or with a beautiful reply.'

Because there will come to you one who is neither human nor Jinn, an Angel from the Angels of the Beneficent, who will test you regarding what I have bestowed upon you and ask you about what I have given you.
So see how you are dealing, O son of Imran.
ai.seo_question: Why should one honour a beggar even with a small gift or kind words?
ai.summary: In this *munajat* (divine whisper) recorded in *Al-Kafi*, Allah instructs Prophet Musa (AS) to honor the beggar with either a modest gift or a gracious reply, emphasizing that the quality of one's response is as meritorious as the material act itself. The narration highlights a unique eschatological or worldly test where an Angel of the Beneficent, distinct from humans and Jinn, observes these interactions to evaluate how Musa manages the blessings (*nu'um*) Allah has granted him. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that charity is not merely transactional but a spiritual trial of gratitude and humility before the Divine.
